newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares stable in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares stable in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose for the fourth day in a row in quiet business on Thursday.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index added 1.31 points to 335.23 in below-average trade of 37.9 million pounds ($11.2 million).
"It's poor volume for Egypt," said Bassim Arida of Prime Investments. "People are staying out, not knowing where to go."
"Nothing was spectacular in the market today. But prices are expected to have reached their bottom and will fluctuate sideways between now and mid-September," he added.
"Prices are very cheap and attractive now for all good shares," Arida said.
The always busy Commercial International Bank/CIB was the day's most active share, closing 0.26 pounds up at 72.75. About 5.4 million pounds were traded.
Suez Cement, one of the favourite cement firms, added 0.25 pounds to close at 64.25, when equity worth 2.8 million pounds changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 446.89 points from 446.29 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 251.23 from 249.93.
Of the 96 shares traded, 44 rose, 29 ended lower and 23 remained unchanged.
